question.problem: A curve is defined by the parametric equations $x=\frac{{t}^{3}}{3},\,y={t}^{5}+2{t}^{3}$ where $t$ is a real number. Calculate $\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}.$
question.worked_solution:
To find the first derivative, we will use the formula

$$
\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{{y}^{′}(t)}{{x}^{′}(t)}.
$$

Differentiating $x$ and $y,$ we get

$$
{x}^{′}(t)={t}^{2},\,{y}^{′}(t)=5{t}^{4}+6{t}^{2}.
$$

 

Therefore,

$$
\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{5{t}^{4}+6{t}^{2}}{{t}^{2}}=5{t}^{2}+6.
$$

To compute the second derivative, we can use the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}} & =\frac{\frac{d}{dt}(\frac{dy}{dx})}{(\frac{dx}{dt})}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting into the formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}} & =\frac{\frac{d}{dt}(5{t}^{2}+6)}{{t}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{10t}{{t}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{10}{t}.\end{aligned}
$$
